answer.answer: Audit-ready reconciliation completed and checkpointed without creating a second canonical game-data snapshot.

claims.value: The lossless import preserves the original 21,674,717-byte ZIP with SHA-256 1a1c1ef0ae00905ced37f1221ab22c4b9268f2ebe17b7516e6c9cac67d7f6fa3 and a verified extracted tree under Git-ignored raw/. The archive has 123 entries including directories, with 115 manifested files plus CHECKSUMS.sha256; unzip -t and every packaged SHA-256 passed. MANIFEST.csv and CHECKSUMS.sha256 remain tracked for auditing. Retrieval occurred at 2026-07-08T19:01:37Z and import at 2026-07-11T19:54:52Z.

The archive’s repeated attribution of numeric data to Steam build 23761620 is unsupported: that identifier represents only the latest observed public executable, Update 1 Hotfix 0.2.8. The source/game-data axis is Update 1 internal version 35118973, dated 2026-04-09 and contextually mapped to Steam build 22674441; the capture axis is canonical SRDB 2.3.4 snapshot ea-u1-gv35118973__srdb-2.3.4__20260711T050230Z, captured 2026-07-11. Imported numeric reports remain legacy calculations until rerun against that snapshot.

No competing game-data snapshot was created. The canonical corpus already covered all 468 archive items, 191 public buildings, 234 recipe definitions, 6 corporations, 77 Corporation levels, 121 export offers, 15 development upgrades, 3,259 map markers, and 3,094 loot entries. Selective promotion was limited to models/rourke-update1-save-baseline__20260711.json, six Ore Excavator v2 recipe/producer associations in sources/recipe-producer-overrides.json, assumptions in sources/consumable-effects.json, nine player-specific site/geography assets, and consolidated player-save, architecture, geography, progression, exploration, food, and remote-resource notes. Reconciliation also corrected the airlock item/building collision and normalized Training Corporation’s literal $undefined index to null.

The complete 18-file Flowworks Campaign Sizing - Levels 8 to 15 family is rejected audit history only and must not become current guidance. Active staged guidance reaches a level-10 cell with one Stabilizer, one Nozzle, one Impeller, two Valves, one Turbine, and two Pumps; the second Stabilizer comes later, while HRS v2 is an evidence-triggered recovery option rather than an initial build. The archived SQLite database, source snapshot JSON, core delivery CSVs, workbook, refresh script, and query script remain preserved only under raw/; the active RuptureOps pipeline and database are authoritative.

claims.value: Active sites: Landerworks (`LW`) is the dependable legacy Rotor, Stator, and Applicator exporter beside the initial lander; Sunstone Station (`LW-SA`) is its active satellite supplying raw Calcium Ore and substantial solar generation. Faraday Works (`FW`) is the rebuilt two-Core Titanium/Wolfram/Helium electrochem Works immediately north of CRRO “Warm Dawn”; it imports Rotor, Stator, and Applicator from Landerworks. Brimstone Utility (`FW-BU`) is Faraday’s active critical satellite, supplying processed Calcium, Sulfur Ore, and all generation. answer.answer: Little Cloud is manageable, but protect the valuable load: bank excess supplies if storage is reasonably close; otherwise use the tagged chamber cautiously and move methodically. Starry Night is easier—clear wanderers, take the final chest first, then loot debris.

claims.value: Little Cloud is about 2/5 difficulty, with 13 persistent hostile spawn entries within 250 units: 8 tier-1 melee, 4 tier-1 ranged, and 1 tier-1 exploder. No Goliaths, Flingers, tier-2 enemies, or raid-class concentration are mapped there; the markers indicate possible persistent population, not 13 simultaneous attackers.

Bank excess valuable ammunition and consumables first if returning to storage is reasonably quick. Otherwise, proceed methodically toward Starry Night using the nearby tagged Regeneration Chamber as limited recovery support—not as a replacement for spare equipment and a safely staged recovery cache.

A claimed nearby Regeneration Chamber can shorten the return trip, but it does not provide replacement weapons, ammunition, healing, or rebuilding materials. Keep those supplies in a safe cache outside the contested base’s corruption failure domain: one observed corruption event disabled both a base and its chamber, sending the next respawn to the starting launcher. This is evidence from one encounter; the exact corruption threshold and general chamber-disable rules remain unverified.

Starry Night is about 1/5 difficulty, with zero persistent hostile spawn markers within 250 units, though roaming enemies can still wander in. Its guaranteed final chest contains an Electronics Blueprint, Rotor Blueprint, 15 Armory Tokens, and a Frame Memory Module; clear wanderers, open that chest first, then loot the debris.

checkpoint.objective: Provide an evidence-backed Little Cloud-to-Starry Night field brief while protecting carried supplies.
current_state: All four requested facets are verified.
Checkpoint checkpoint:019fa494-03e0-7be3-9db9-ea7efd4da492 was committed.
decisions: Recommend banking excess supplies when storage is reasonably close; otherwise advance methodically with a safely staged recovery cache.
Treat the observed corruption-related chamber failure as historical field evidence, not a universal mechanic.
next_actions: No further retrieval is required for this brief.

answer.answer: The first Geo Scanner lesson is now preserved as durable operational guidance with observation, generalization, and loot uncertainty kept distinct.

claims.value: The first activation caused two deaths before success. After the first death, the player respawned at a nearby claimed base, but it lacked replacement weapons and materials, forcing a walk back to Landerworks. On the second attempt, the scanner fire base had a claimed Regeneration Chamber, but its turrets were unpowered and provided no defense; after the player was overwhelmed, corruption disabled the base and chamber, so the next respawn occurred at the starting launcher.

Success came from returning with a fully built-out temporary fire base and powering every turret. The automated defense continuously engaged the wave—the turrets were described as “singing”—and the scanner was completed.

The unpowered-turret failure, corruption of the contested base, loss of its claimed Regeneration Chamber, and fallback to the starting launcher are direct field observations from one encounter. They do not establish a universal corruption threshold or complete Regeneration Chamber disable/availability rule.

For future scanners: treat activation as a deliberate defense event; claim a nearby Regeneration Chamber but assume the contested base can fail; power every turret and verify tracking/firing before activation; keep replacement weapons, ammunition, healing, and rebuilding materials in a separate safe cache outside the corruption/failure area; and preserve a route to a stable production base or launcher. The completed site appeared to yield two unusually good food-related rewards or stacks, possibly involving a quantity of 20, but the dictated report is ambiguous, so exact items and counts remain unresolved. The scanner identity and coordinates are also unknown.
source_paths: Topics/StarRupture/Player save - sites and freight network.md

answer.answer: Faraday field plan preserved with route, goals, low-twitch constraints, and permanent food system intact.

claims.value: Launch from Faraday immediately north of CRRO “Warm Dawn.” Outing 1: post-Rupture caves, then Warm Dawn → Grey Owl → Lemon Souls → Purple Haze. Outing 2: Little Cloud → Starry Night → optional scanner → Mythic Cry/Grand Basin; survey rather than build while progression-gated. Outing 3: Forgotten Engine. Run Redleaf afterward only if Turbine/Electromagnetic Coil blueprints remain blockers.
source_paths: Topics/StarRupture/Player save - progression and next builds.md

claims.value: Keep the complete queue active: blueprints and map reveal; Quartz and War Bonds for the Machine Gun; permanent low-chore food; conservative Forgotten Engine completion; later Goethite and Oil supply; and directions grounded in the player’s named landmarks.

Plan for a low-twitch player: shotgun for close waves/corridors; accurate rifle for Flingers, Spitters, and controlled ranged fire; favor doors, cover, retreats, line-of-sight breaks, and shields over open DPS races. Stage ammunition and healing, preserve a manual-save safety point and abort route, and do not depend on cross-planet ammunition delivery during combat. SLAMS-12, MAR-9, M175, LEM, mods, and other suggested equipment are recommendations—not confirmed ownership; verify the live loadout before asserting ownership.

Permanent three-item system: prevention—Nutri Block, 5 Prickler + 1 Oxallop → 1; stops calorie/hydration drain for 30 minutes, adds 45 toxicity, and should be used from full meters at low toxicity. Calorie recovery—5 Polufruit + 1 Prism Herb → 3 Calorie Chews, restoring 40 calories each. Hydration recovery—4 Hydrobulb + 1 Prism Herb → 1 Aqua Chew, restoring 100 hydration. Standard refill: 3 Calorie Chews + 1 Aqua Chew, restoring 120 calories and 100 hydration across two stacks. Figler is too laborious for routine use; retain Glowcaps as strategic combat-medicine reserve.

answer.answer: Watch Session remains a proposed, evidence-bounded Mission Timeline design—not a verified install-ready app. Its honest MVP centers on a large next-event countdown, conservative threat language, separately versioned opportunities, explicit confidence, and opt-in native alerts.

claims.value: The design is pinned to Early Access Update 1 through Hotfix 0.2.8, Steam build 23761620, released 2026-06-17, and SRDB 2.3.4 captured 2026-07-11. Its 54-minute impact-to-impact cycle is a strongly corroborated community/game-data model, not an official Creepy Jar formula. Use predicted/expected/favorable/lower threat—not exact/safe/guaranteed—until live validation. Mission Timeline was selected at 2026-07-11 22:54 UTC, but historical evidence shows no final handoff or proof that simulator/install-ready acceptance passed.

claims.value: Expose five player-facing states: Fire wave 0:00-0:30 (remain sheltered), Cooling 0:30-1:30 (remain sheltered), Recovery / quiet window 1:30-11:30 (lower ambient threat; use the window), World active 11:30-51:30 (ordinary enemies and ecology active), and Ruptura warning 51:30-54:00 (return, bank loot, shelter). Anchor 0:00 when the local fire wall reaches the player. The hero is a huge across-the-room countdown to the next meaningful event: expected ordinary-Vermin return during recovery, otherwise the next warning/Ruptura. Keep sync/capability state, semantic state, countdown target, threat/action instruction, at most two opportunities, and exact-time next events visible without scrolling. Preserve a proportional overview, but add minimum-width labeled steps or an event list so short phases remain legible.
source_paths: Projects/RuptureOps/Rupture cycle timer - research and product design.md

claims.value: Opportunities are separately versioned evidence records—not phase mechanics—with an ID, start/end event or offset, action and caveat, evidence class/confidence, applicable game build, and source snapshot. Initial evidence supports recovery-oriented cards for reduced ordinary POI population, dry-lakebed Oxallop, cave access/Quartz/Glowcaps, post-cooling Ignitium, experimental late-recovery Star Tears, and variable Coralion/Vulpir eggs; regrowth foliage/water gets non-exact wording, while Sulheart stays hidden pending validation. Every card must say confirmed, community-derived, player-observed, or experimental and preserve caveats. In particular, surface the choice that Star Tears mature on unharvested cooled Ignitium instead of promising both harvests simultaneously. Triggered Geo Scanner, monolith, infection, Base Core, and scripted POI encounters may ignore the environmental cycle.
source_paths: Projects/RuptureOps/Rupture cycle timer - research and product design.md

claims.value: Enemy-return and Ruptura alerts require distinct sounds and haptics and must never depend on color or audio alone. Enemy-return defaults are 5 minutes (amber edge, finish/leave hard POIs, short double haptic, optional tone, local notification), 2 minutes (persistent retreat banner, double tone/haptic, optional notification), 1 minute (red instruction and emphasized seconds, background cue off by default), 15 seconds (static danger border, large seconds, one final cue, no ticking), and the event (ORDINARY VERMIN RETURNING, urgent triple cue, notification or explicitly armed alarm). Ruptura supports optional 10 minutes, then 5 minutes, 2:30, 1 minute, 30 seconds, 15 seconds, and impact; an exit buffer may trigger TURN BACK NOW earlier. Preserve Full/Haptic only/Visual only profiles, separate toggles, Mute one cycle, preview, visible capability state and next-alert time. Use absolute dates, reschedule after anchor/model/policy changes, recompute from (now - anchor) modulo cycle duration on resume, deduplicate by cycle number plus event ID, and collapse missed cues to the strongest current state. Disable the idle timer only while monitoring and restore it; never use background audio as keep-alive. Use a Live Activity only for the armed next event. AlarmKit requires explicit authorization and deliberate arming—never an endless 54-minute alarm. Earlier iOS uses normal notifications; Time Sensitive is opt-in and Critical Alerts are inappropriate. Preserve Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, high contrast, Differentiate Without Color, Reduce Motion, stable VoiceOver summaries, and no flashing or default per-second ticking.

Public release requires a clean separation from private corpus and player material, followed by explicit permission or licensed replacement data and independently cleared assets.

claims.value: The third-party source permits crawling but publishes no explicit data/content reuse license. Its mirrored raw archive, normalized corpus, and derived SQLite database remain private research assets and must not be placed in a public repository or build.

Only import manifests and promoted facts carrying explicit provenance belong in version control; that allowance does not itself grant public-distribution rights.

A clean public implementation may presently draw on the independently authored native domain, service, and test work recorded under `ios/`, including AlertPlanner, RuptureCycle, RuptureCycleDefinitions, WatchSession, ForegroundFeedbackController, NotificationService, ScreenAwakeController, and their unit/UI tests—but only after separating them from private data and assets. Binary site images, player screenshots, the generated/original app icon, phase-color resources, and four original warning sounds for hostiles and Ruptura have no demonstrated public clearance here and must remain private or be replaced/cleared.

Before broader distribution, obtain explicit data/content reuse permission from the third-party source owner or replace the corpus with a separately licensed data strategy. Build a clean public target that excludes the mirrored raw archive, normalized corpus, SQLite database, duplicate imported corpus, prompt history, save/player models, screenshots/site images, generated app icon, phase-color resources, and warning audio unless each item is independently licensed or authorship-cleared.
